newsitem.title: USA: American Air swamped with calls after fare slashing.
newsitem.headline: American Air swamped with calls after fare slashing.

text.p: American Airlines has been swamped with customer calls after slashing its fares as much as 50 percent over the weekend, company officials said on Monday.
Spokesman Tim Smith said up to 2.5 million people called American's reservation switchboards on Monday alone, way up from the 340,000 calls the airline receives on an average day.
"The exact numbers aren't available yet but several hundred thousand new bookings and reservations have been taken since late Sunday," Smith said.

American cut its fares in half and doubled frequent flier mile credits early on Saturday, minutes after President Bill Clinton forced striking pilots back to work by appointing a presidential board to draw up a proposed solution to the bitter labor dispute between pilots and management.

The fare sale was aimed at winning back tens of thousands of strike-wary customers who had booked flights on other airlines, and has sparked a fare war with other airlines forced to match American's offers.
American's 9,300 pilots walked off the job at midnight on Friday but Clinton stepped in within minutes, using emergency powers to appoint the presidential board.

The move forced the pilots back to work just 24 minutes into their strike and postponed any new walkout for 60 days. A strike would have cost American, a unit of Fort Worth, Texas-based AMR Corp. upwards of $30 million a day and the U.S. economy $100 million to $200 million a day.
Pilots were angered by Clinton's intervention and have warned they will strike again in 60 days unless American meets their wage and contract demands.
